raised_by: CC, during the 2026-08-15 deep review — the loop measured itself older than the code it judges at 2026-08-14 23:14 (9 occurrences), its own record said 'restart the loop', and nine-plus hours later it was the same stale pid at 65% CPU. The detector worked; nothing owned the actuator. CC restarted it by hand (pid 897888 -> 3592949) and cleared the trouble through the device door.
question: When the ground loop measures ITSELF stale, who performs the restart — does the loop exec itself into the new code, does the trouble it raises fire a restart at a holder, or does it stay a hand act?
whats_beyond: The staleness voyage (the-ground-loop-names-its-own-staleness-instead-of-benching-a-device, PROVED 2026-08-14) deliberately built the NAMING half only: the loop stops blaming devices for its own age. The restart half was left unbuilt, and the first live firing showed the cost: the watch layer ran dark-while-looking-alive overnight. Self-exec is the smallest mechanism (the process already knows the verdict and its own argv) but a process that replaces itself on its own diagnosis needs a guard against exec loops; a trouble-fired restart routes through a holder that does not exist yet (system_rackmount is the host-predicate owner, not a supervisor — and no-enforcer-gated-ownership warns against inventing one). A hand act is where it stands today, measured working exactly once.

resolved.answer: Nobody owns a restart, because for the code the loop SERVES there is no longer a restart to own: presence is the subscription. A component's groundloop/pulse.py is found each beat, imported on appearance, and unloaded from sys.modules on disappearance — identity is path+mtime, so a changed file is remove+add within one beat. The loop holds nothing that can go stale for pulse-carried code; the disk is the roster. Measured live 2026-08-15: a dropped pulse served in 2.12s, a removed one unloaded in ~3s, same pid throughout. RESIDUE, bounded and named in the ticket's distinctions: the loop's own spine (loop.py, discovery.py, the shim) still ships by deployment restart — exercised exactly once this voyage (pid 3592949 -> 3933751, the launcher's own spawn line, singleton guard deciding). That residue is a deployment act, not a supervisor: no-enforcer-gated-ownership stands, and self-exec stays unbuilt until a lived symptom asks for it.
